[Elastic{ON}](https://www.elastic.co/events/elasticon) kicks off this September with seven stops in cities around the world, running through March 2027:


[Mumbai](https://www.elastic.co/events/elasticon/mumbai) ,


[New York](https://www.elastic.co/events/elasticon/new-york-city) ,


[Amsterdam](https://www.elastic.co/events/elasticon/amsterdam) ,


[San Francisco](https://www.elastic.co/events/elasticon/san-francisco-ai) , London, Washington, DC, Singapore, and a final digital event. The annual tour has been a fixture of the Elastic community since the early days back when the platform was more commonly known as the ELK Stack, growing from grassroots developer meetups into the global practitioner event series it is today.


## Forge the future: Make all your data an AI advantage


The more powerful AI gets, the more your data is worth. That’s true whether you're a developer building something that needs to understand the world around it, an SRE diagnosing what broke and why, or a security analyst chasing a threat through millions of events. Elastic’s CEO Ash Kulkarni will be appearing at stops across the tour, opening keynotes with a candid conversation about why your data has never been more valuable and how an evolved Elasticsearch will make your observability, security, and AI applications smarter, faster, and more efficient.


### For builders and developers


If you've shipped an AI application that worked and then watched it fall apart in production, the problem is likely context. Getting reliable, accurate context into an AI agent at scale is harder than it looks, and the gap between a working prototype and a production-ready app is where most teams get stuck.


This year's search track will show you how Elasticsearch helps you scale agents in production with context that's reliable, token efficient, and current. Agent responses stay accurate, and the AI experiences you ship stay reliable as workloads grow. This year's Elastic{ON} is where developers can figure out how to give production the context the demo took for granted.


### For SREs and platform engineers


Most SREs have a story about a night when everything went sideways at once. The question isn't whether incidents will happen; it's whether your tooling can handle them before they wake up the entire team.


This year’s observability track will spotlight how significant investments in both logging and metrics can help you keep more of the signals you need (while spending less) and will give you a sneak peek into how Elastic's forthcoming AI SRE will autonomously detect, investigate, and resolve incidents. A future devoid of 3:00 a.m. alerts is closer than it sounds after all. This year's Elastic{ON} is where SREs can figure out what to do when their observability data is growing faster than their team can manage it.


### For security analysts and SOC teams


Every SOC analyst knows the feeling where the queue never stops growing. Attacks land in minutes, and the alert that matters is buried under a thousand that don't.


The Elastic{ON} security track shows how your team can shift from working the queue to deciding on the work. It starts with the opening keynote, where agents run continuous detection, investigation, and correlation and then deliver evidence-backed proposals for humans to act on. The track also covers continuous threat hunting that surfaces what analysts would have missed; expanded Attack Discovery and alert analysis workflows that hand analysts pre-triaged findings; agentic endpoint operations that retire manual tool-chaining; and native security intelligence that turns research into customer protections. All of it is built to augment your SOC, not replace it. A day spent making decisions instead of chasing alerts is closer than most teams expect.


## What to expect


Every stop will have:


-


A keynote


-


Three practitioner-focused breakout tracks across search, security, and observability


-


Hands-on workshops


-


Customer stories


-


Live demonstrations


-


A look at what's arriving in Elastic's next release


-


An evening networking reception


## What's not on the agenda


Some of the best things about Elastic{ON} don't show up on the agenda. It's the hallway conversations and the chance meetings with a former colleague or a peer from across the industry. The "small world" moments where you realize that despite how many winding roads there are in tech, Elasticsearch keeps bringing like-minded people back into the same room. These meetings and conversations are always worth the trip.


## What you’ll walk away with


Attendees tend to leave Elastic{ON} thinking differently about data — not just the structured kind in an old-school database, but the stuff being generated everywhere constantly, like call transcripts, observability streams, security telemetry, and agent traces. It’s the data that's already there and mostly going unused.


What if your sales team's call recordings could actually shape what your CRM tells you about a deal? What if those unused logs weren't just a storage cost but a critical signal? With Elasticsearch, there's no hard ceiling on how data can be put to work. And Elastic{ON} is where you learn how to do it.
